messages:
alex: observed a regression in p99 tail latency when speculative decoding is enabled for the Mistral->Qwen draft pairing. started after last runtime bump. traces show repeated KV cache evictions and a fallback to a slower kernel on sequence lengths > 2048.

maria: can you paste the perf profile? is it kernel selection or memory thrash? :thinking: 

alex: pasted a small excerpt from perf-top: 

```
# perf sample summary
kernels: 'attn_fwd_opt' 22%  (fast)
kernels: 'attn_fwd_generic' 48% (slow)
cuda_memcpy 14%
kv_cache_invalidate 9%
other 7%
```

alex: the runtime is choosing attn_fwd_generic for Mixtral-family variants even though we've got optimized kernels available for Mistral-ish shapes. suspected cause: shape mismatch after RoPE scaling for Mixtral head dims.

jin: how are we computing the handshake for draft pairing? if tokenizer mismatch occurs, acceptance rate drops and we keep speculating which increases load. also we have a tokenization mismatch patch in staging that could cause a double-bos on mixtral -> qwen.

caroline: added the CI perf test link: https://ci.internal/redwood/runtime/branches/runtime-bump-2026/build/487/perf-report. shows 12% p99 regression on longcontext workload with speculative enabled.

alex: reproduction script i used (local):
```
# repro.sh
python3 tools/bench_speculative.py \
  --model primary=mistral-mixtral-14b \
  --draft=qwen-14b \
  --seq-len 4096 \
  --speculative true \
  --accept-threshold 0.85
```

maria: interesting — acceptance threshold 0.85 is pretty high; that will cause fallback traffic if tokenizers disagree. what's the observed acceptance rate?

alex: acceptance rate dropped to ~60% on mixed-domain prompts. logs: 
```
acceptance_rates: {
  prompt_type_A: 0.82,
  prompt_type_B: 0.57,
  prompt_type_C: 0.29
}
```

sri: low acceptance + KV thrash = kernel recompile churn and cache eviction. two orthogonal fixes: 1) validate family/tokenizer compatibility before pairing (fast check), 2) improve batching heuristic to avoid mixing long seqs with short ones when speculative is on.

jin: +1 on tokenizer handshake. propose we add a preflight: compare tokenizer.vocab_hash or sample-encode("\n") across models, fail fast if mismatch. also fallback should prefer same-family model with compatible RoPE base.

caroline: on the kernel side, we should log chosen kernel and shape at runtime when a non-optimized kernel is used. that will make it easier to tie RoPE/heads/kv dims to kernel selection. can add an opt-in env var REDWOOD_VERBOSE_KERNEL=1.

alex: i already hacked a quick trace: found calls where kv_cache_invalidate happened each decode step for mixtral drafts — looks like kv key shape toggles between [bs, heads, seq, dim] variants because we had inconsistent kv-dtype/transpose in the draft model loader. patch incoming.

maria: nice. can we also tune the acceptance scoring to be position-aware? we accept early tokens more aggressively but for RoPE-different families maybe require higher confidence for first 5 tokens. would reduce harmful rollbacks.

jin: we should run two targeted experiments: 
- A: disable speculative for mixtral->qwen and measure p99 delta
- B: keep speculative but enable family-handshake + tokenizer-check + REDWOOD_VERBOSE_KERNEL and rerun perf.

alex: scheduled both. running A now. will post numbers.

ci-bot: perf test A finished: p99 improved by 10% when speculative disabled for that pairing (build 489). link: https://ci.internal/redwood/runtime/489/results

alex: result A confirms hypothesis. B still running (long).

caroline: next steps: 1) enable tokenizer family handshake for runtime pairing (opt-out), 2) add kernel shape logs behind env flag, 3) patch kv loader to canonicalize shapes/dtypes, 4) add an acceptance-rate tuning knob per-family in spec config. I'll file infra tickets and assign.

maria: thanks. also add a small unit test that encodes a few edge-case tokens across models to fail fast in CI.

alex: filed: https://tickets.internal/redwood/RT-2321 Speculative: family-handshake + kv canonicalize + kernel-logs. assigning to eng-runtime.

sri: triage note — low-risk toggle first (handshake), then kernel logs, then kv patch. plan looks good. :thumbsup:

alex: will follow up with B results and a microprofiling trace for kernel devs. thanks all.
